# Rename section text to `content` and key generation tasks by section id

**Goal:** Report sections are stored under `content` and generated by section id, with no failed reads, dropped tasks or duplicate paid calls while the change rolls out.

## Problem Statement

Each report is made of sections whose text is written by a paid model call that runs from a background queue. Today the stored text lives under an old name, and each queued job finds its section by its display name, which is not guaranteed to be unique and can silently match no section at all. Renaming the stored field and switching jobs to the section's id fixes the naming and the lookup, but done naively on the live service it would break report reads and drop or repeat paid generations during the deploy, which costs the user missing sections (priority 1, user experience) and wasted paid calls (priority 2, cost).

Evidence from the live tree:

| Fact | Anchor |
| --- | --- |
| Section text column is `body`; `name` has no uniqueness constraint per report | migrations/001_reports.sql:8-14 |
| Reads select `body` and the HTTP response spreads it as the `body` key | src/db.ts:12, src/app.ts:14 |
| Writes match on `report_id` + `name`, so a duplicate name updates several rows and a missing name updates zero rows while the task still reports `ok` | src/db.ts:16, src/worker.ts:10-11 |
| Task payload is `{ reportId, section }` where `section` is the name | src/queue.ts:11, src/worker.ts:6 |
| `enqueueSection` has no caller in this repo, so the task producer may live elsewhere | src/queue.ts:4 (grep finds no other reference) |
| `deploy.sh` never applies migrations, so schema and code cannot land atomically | deploy.sh:1-4 |
| Each generation call takes 20-60 s and costs money; there is no timeout and a non-2xx answer is saved as the section text | src/llm.ts:1-11 |

## Request vetting

- **Hypothesis:** The rename and the id-keyed task can ship with zero failed reads, zero dropped tasks and a safe rollback, provided the rename is staged (add `content` and dual-write now, drop `body` later) and the worker accepts both the old name-keyed and the new id-keyed payload.
- **Case against:** Done literally as one in-place column rename plus one payload swap, it breaks in production: old revisions still query `body` [anchor: src/db.ts:12], tasks already queued carry only the name [anchor: src/queue.ts:11] so a worker reading `sectionId` gets `undefined`, a rollback to the previous revision would receive id-only tasks it cannot parse, and `deploy.sh` applies no migrations [anchor: deploy.sh:4] so there is always a window where schema and code disagree. The column rename itself buys only naming; the id switch is the part with real value.
- **Sources:** https://martinfowler.com/bliki/ParallelChange.html
- **Verdict:** adopt-with-conditions: ship only the expand phase — `content` added and dual-written, API key unchanged, worker accepts payload v1 and v2 — so the rollout records zero failed section reads; dropping `body` and v1 support waits for the contract follow-up.

## Existing-code assessment

- **migrations/001_reports.sql:** keep — schema history is append-only; the change lands as a new idempotent `002` file [anchor: migrations/001_reports.sql:8]
- **src/db.ts:** keep — three small query functions; extend in place with id-keyed lookup and save, and rename the name-keyed save to mark it legacy [anchor: src/db.ts:15]
- **src/queue.ts:** keep — single producer function; extend the payload with a version field and the id, add a timeout and a status check [anchor: src/queue.ts:4]
- **src/worker.ts:** keep — 8-line handler; add a payload parser in front and an id-keyed branch [anchor: src/worker.ts:5]
- **src/llm.ts:** keep — add a timeout and a non-2xx guard to `generateSection` only; `suggestTitle` is untouched [anchor: src/llm.ts:2]

## Scope Boundary

**In scope:**

- New column `content` on `sections`, backfilled from `body`, read by the service and written alongside `body` (expand phase).
- Generate-section task payload v2 `{ version: 2, reportId, sectionId, section }`, where `section` (the name) stays as a transitional field for rollback safety.
- Worker accepts v2 (looks the section up by id) and v1 (legacy name lookup, today's behavior).
- Bundled fixes on the touched path: generation call timeout, non-2xx model answers no longer saved as section text, enqueue timeout and status check, queue dispatch deadline and max attempts, no paid call for a deleted section.
- First metrics contract for the worker, including a payload-version counter that tells the operator when v1 tasks have stopped arriving.

**Out of scope:**

- Dropping `body`, stopping the dual-write, removing v1 support and the transitional `section` field (contract follow-up, candidate 1).
- Renaming the `body` key in the `GET /reports/:id` JSON response (Open Question Q2).
- Authenticating the task endpoint (candidate 2) and skip-on-redelivery idempotency (candidate 3).
- Spend caps and a migration runner.

## Behavioral contrast

### User flow

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A report reader gets each section's text under `body` | Unchanged: same `body` key, now read from `content` |
| A model call that errors saves blank text into the section and the job ends as done | The job fails and the queue retries it; the section fills once a call succeeds |
| A model call that hangs holds the job until the queue's 10-minute deadline | The call is abandoned after 120 s and retried |
| A job for a deleted section still pays for a generation that is then discarded | The job ends immediately with no paid call |

### System flow

- **Before:**
  - Section text lives only in `sections.body`.
  - The task carries `{ reportId, section: <name> }`; the worker generates first, then updates every row matching that name (zero or several).
  - No metrics exist.
- **After:**
  - `sections.content` is the column of record; `body` is written in lockstep as a rollback mirror.
  - The producer emits `{ version: 2, reportId, sectionId, section: <name> }`; the worker resolves the section by id before any paid call and writes exactly one row.
  - Payload v1 is still accepted and handled exactly as before (name match, dual-write).
  - The worker emits duration, failure and payload-version metrics through a new in-memory helper.

**Lost:** nothing for report readers; deprecated: `body` becomes a mirror column, the name-keyed save and v1 payload become legacy-only paths, all scheduled for removal in the contract follow-up.

## User Stories / Acceptance Criteria

### Story 1: Schema expands without breaking running code

- [ ] Given a database with migration 001 and rows in `sections`, when migration 002 is applied twice, then `content` exists, every row has `content = body`, and the second run updates zero rows (local Postgres smoke in Test Steps, exit code 0).
- [ ] Given migration 002 is applied and the previous revision is still serving, when it reads or writes sections, then it succeeds because `body` is untouched (002 contains no `rename` or `drop`: `! grep -qiE 'rename|drop' migrations/002_sections_content.sql`).

### Story 2: Id-keyed tasks

- [ ] Given a v2 payload for an existing section, when the worker runs, then it calls the model once with the section's name and saves by id (`bun test src/worker.test.ts`).
- [ ] Given a v2 payload whose `sectionId` does not exist or belongs to another report, when the worker runs, then it responds 200 without calling the model (`bun test src/worker.test.ts`).
- [ ] Given the producer builds a task, then the payload has `version: 2`, `sectionId` and the transitional `section` name (`bun test src/queue.test.ts`).

### Story 3: Legacy tasks keep working

- [ ] Given a v1 payload `{ reportId, section }`, when the worker runs, then it saves by report id + name exactly as today, writing both columns (`bun test src/worker.test.ts`).
- [ ] Given a payload with neither `sectionId` nor `section`, when the worker runs, then it responds 200 with no model call and records `error.type=invalid_input` (`bun test src/worker.test.ts`).

### Story 4: Model failures retry instead of blanking a section

- [ ] Given the model API answers non-2xx or exceeds 120 s, when the worker runs, then nothing is saved and the worker responds 500 so the queue retries (`bun test src/worker.test.ts src/llm.test.ts`).

### Story 5: Report reads are unchanged

- [ ] Given sections with `content`, when `GET /reports/:id` is served, then each section still carries `id`, `name`, `body` (`grep -q 'coalesce(content, body) as body' src/db.ts` plus the local Postgres smoke).

## Instrumentation

**Contract:** `.flow/metrics.md` create

### Metrics

| Metric | Instrument | Unit | Attributes (closed values) | Emitted at |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reports.generate_section.duration` | Histogram | seconds | `operation.outcome` (`ok`, `error`) | generate-section worker |
| `reports.generate_section.failures` | Counter | none | `error.type` (`_OTHER`, `internal`, `invalid_input`, `not_found`, `upstream_error`, `upstream_timeout`) | generate-section worker |
| `reports.generate_section.payloads` | Counter | `{task}` | `task.payload_version` (`1`, `2`) | generate-section worker, on parse |
| Cloud Tasks `queue/depth` | Gauge | `{message}` | `messaging.destination.name` (`sections`) | platform-native (Cloud Tasks) |

Explicit histogram boundaries (job-scale, not request-scale): `[1, 5, 10, 20, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120]`.

Estimated series: 32 per operation (histogram 2 x (9 + 3) = 24, failures 6, payloads 2; per instance)

**Attributes:** new keys added as `.flow/metrics.md` `## Attributes` rows — `operation.outcome` (`ok`, `error`), `error.type` (list above), `task.payload_version` (`1`, `2`; temporary, removed with v1 support), `messaging.destination.name` (`sections`).

### Error types

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `_OTHER` | fallback: no listed class fits |
| `internal` | unexpected failure inside the service (for example a database error) |
| `invalid_input` | the task payload has neither `sectionId` nor `section`, or the id belongs to another report (client-caused) |
| `not_found` | the report or section no longer exists (client-caused) |
| `upstream_error` | the model API answered non-2xx or without text |
| `upstream_timeout` | the model API did not answer within 120 s |

### Dashboard panels

Added to `.flow/metrics.md` `## Dashboard panels`, all on the `reports-service overview` dashboard (spec-only):

- Section generation p50/p95 duration by `operation.outcome`.
- Section generation failures by `error.type`.
- Generate-section tasks by `task.payload_version` (the v1 line reaching zero is the contract-phase signal).
- `sections` queue depth (platform-native).

### Alerts

burn-rate tiers only

### SLO

New journey SLO `section generation`: SLI = share of generate-section tasks ending `ok`, excluding client-caused `not_found` and `invalid_input`; target 99% over 28 days. First SLO in the repo — no existing journey to roll into.

**As-code:** spec-only — the repo keeps no dashboard or alert files and has no metrics backend yet (`none yet — suggested: Google Cloud Monitoring`).

## Architecture Decisions

| Aspect | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Layers touched | DB schema (new migration), persistence (`src/db.ts`), queue producer (`src/queue.ts`), queue consumer (`src/worker.ts`), outbound model client (`src/llm.ts`), new metrics helper |
| Domain modules | Existing: db, queue, worker, llm. New: `src/metrics.ts` (single-purpose, zero dependencies, per AGENTS.md) |
| Data flow | Producer enqueues `{version, reportId, sectionId, section}` → Cloud Tasks → worker parses (v2 or v1) → id lookup → model call → one-row dual-write of `content` and `body`; reads serve `coalesce(content, body)` as `body` |
| Pattern | Expand/contract (parallel change) for the column; versioned, tolerant-reader task payload. Both are new to this repo, justified by the absence of a migration runner and by tasks surviving deploys |
| Binary-framing check | Rename-in-place vs. full expand/contract has a middle: in-place rename behind a `--no-traffic` deploy and a traffic switch (Decision 1). This PR also takes a middle on the payload: v2 adds the id but keeps the name for one release instead of replacing it outright |
| Goal-anchor check | The Goal demands zero failed reads and zero dropped tasks during rollout; the literal "instead of the section name" conflicts with rollback safety, so the name stays as a transitional field (Q3) |

### Runtime design

| Operation | Est. p99 | Execution model | Timeout / deadline | Retries | Idempotency key | Cost bound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Generate-section task (consumer, changed) | ~60 s | existing Cloud Tasks queue `sections` + worker invoked synchronously under the attempt deadline | model call 120 s (new) inside a 300 s per-task dispatch deadline (new) | queue only: max attempts 5, backoff 10-300 s (new, set in deploy.sh); worker never retries | section id (v2); report id + section name (v1); redelivery overwrites the same row | at most 5 paid calls per job (queue max attempts); no spend ledger |
| Enqueue generate-section task (producer, changed) | inline — <1 s, timeout 10 s (new) | | | | | |
| Section reads for `GET /reports/:id` (changed column) | inline — <0.1 s, timeout: database client default (unchanged) | | | | | |
| Migration 002 apply and post-rollout re-apply (operator, one-off) | seconds at current table size | manual `psql` run | none | none; re-runnable by design | idempotent statements (`if not exists`, `is distinct from`) | none — no paid calls |

**Platform:** gcp

**Proportionality:** no migration runner, no spend ledger, no skip-on-redelivery guard and no canary — each is either a separate decision (candidates 2-3) or more than a rename warrants; the one rollout safety measure kept is the expand phase plus the versioned payload.

**Recovery:** section text is paid model output, regenerable at one model call per section; migration 002 is additive and never rewrites `body`. Before applying it the operator takes an on-demand Cloud SQL backup (`gcloud sql backups create --instance <instance>`), and the restore check is `select count(*) from sections where content is distinct from body` returning 0 after the reconcile run.

## Technical Constraints

- Migration 002 must be applied before `./deploy.sh`, because the new revision reads and writes `content`; `deploy.sh` does not apply migrations [deploy.sh:1-4].
- Migration 002's reconcile statement copies `body` into `content` and is only correct while every writer dual-writes; the contract follow-up must stop re-running it before it stops writing `body`.
- The worker must answer 2xx for permanent failures (gone, invalid) and non-2xx only for transient ones, because Cloud Tasks retries every non-2xx; this matches the existing `gone` response [src/worker.ts:8].
- No new runtime dependencies: the metrics helper is an in-memory recorder and tests use `bun test` with `mock.module` [AGENTS.md].
- Cost: the change removes paid calls (deleted sections) and caps retries at 5 attempts per job; model errors that were silently marked done now retry, costing up to 4 extra calls per failing job.
- `gcloud tasks queues create ... || true` never updates an existing queue [deploy.sh:3], so retry settings go in a separate `gcloud tasks queues update` line.

## Open Questions

- [ ] Q1. Stage the rename (add `content`, dual-write, drop `body` later) rather than renaming the column in place? Redirecting to in-place rename collapses Tasks 1-2 into one `alter table ... rename column` and accepts a failure window.
  - **Stakes:** both — if wrong, report reads fail and paid generations retry for the length of the deploy (priority 1 user experience, priority 2 cost)
  - **Recommended:** stage it — the only option with zero failed reads and a working rollback, since migrations are applied by hand outside the deploy [confidence: medium] [anchor: weighing: risk — deploy.sh applies no migrations, so schema and code cannot switch together]
- [ ] Q2. Keep the `GET /reports/:id` response key as `body` while the column becomes `content`? Redirecting renames the API key, which is a breaking change for every reader of the endpoint.
  - **Stakes:** user — any client reading `body` would see sections go blank if the key changes unannounced (priority 1 user experience)
  - **Recommended:** keep `body` in the response — the request names the column only, and an API rename needs its own consumer migration [confidence: medium] [anchor: weighing: reversibility — an alias is free to remove later, a renamed key cannot be un-broken for clients that already failed]
- [ ] Q3. Keep the section name in the v2 payload for one release alongside `sectionId`, deviating from "instead of the section name"? Redirecting removes the `section` field from v2 now.
  - **Stakes:** system — without it, a rollback to the previous revision silently pays for generations it then discards for every id-only task (priority 2 cost, priority 4 quality)
  - **Recommended:** keep it until the contract follow-up — rollback safety outweighs one redundant field [confidence: medium] [anchor: weighing: reversibility — the previous worker reads only `section` and has no guard for its absence]
- [ ] Q4. Apply migration 002 by hand with `psql` before the deploy, then re-apply it once the new revision serves all traffic? Redirecting (for example, an existing runner elsewhere) changes the runbook in the PR and the migration header.
  - **Stakes:** system — if a different process applies migrations, the documented order is wrong and the new revision fails until it runs
  - **Recommended:** manual `psql`, order documented in the migration header and the PR [confidence: high] [anchor: deploy.sh:4]
- [ ] Q5. Abandon a model call after 120 s, give each job a 300 s dispatch deadline, and cap the queue at 5 attempts? Redirecting changes the constants, the deploy.sh queue settings and the histogram's top boundary.
  - **Stakes:** system — too short or too few retries healthy slow calls and gives up early; too long or too many pays for up to N calls per failing section (priority 2 cost)
  - **Recommended:** 120 s / 300 s / 5 attempts — twice the documented 60 s worst case, with deadlines shrinking inward, and a per-job spend ceiling of five calls [confidence: medium] [anchor: adjacent: src/llm.ts:1]
- [x] Should the v2 payload drop `reportId`? — resolved: keep it; see Alternatives considered.
  - **Stakes:** none — resolved without asking

## Decision analysis

**Decision 1 — How does the column rename reach production?** (mutually exclusive branches)

| Branch | End-to-end flow during the deploy | Interruptions per run | Rollback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A. Rename in place, one PR | Operator runs `alter table sections rename column body to content`; until the new revision serves 100% (a `--source` build plus traffic shift, minutes), every report read returns 500 and every worker save fails after its paid call, so the queue retries and pays again | 0 prompts; 1 manual migration step; a failure window of minutes | Needs a reverse rename; previous revision is broken against the new schema |
| B. Middle: rename in place behind `--no-traffic` | Operator deploys with `--no-traffic`, runs the rename, then shifts traffic; the window shrinks to the seconds between rename and shift, but tasks still in flight on the old revision fail and retry | 0 prompts; 3 manual steps (deploy, rename, shift); a failure window of seconds | Same as A |
| C. Expand/contract (this plan) | Operator backs up, applies additive 002, deploys, re-applies 002; old and new revisions both work at every moment | 0 prompts; 3 manual steps now (backup, apply, re-apply) plus one follow-up PR | Previous revision keeps working because `body` is still written |

Ranked: C > B > A. Verdict: **C, expand/contract** — the only branch with no failed reads and a working rollback, at the cost of one follow-up PR [confidence: medium] [anchor: weighing: risk — no migration runner exists, so A and B always leave a window where schema and code disagree].

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep old readers working through a view that exposes `content` as `body`** — rejected: a view cannot share the table name `sections`, which every existing query targets (src/db.ts:12, src/db.ts:16).
- **Carry only `sectionId` and derive the report from the section row** — rejected: the request replaces only the name ("carry the section id instead of the section name"), and `reportId` is already read before the paid call (src/worker.ts:6-8), letting the worker reject a mismatched id cheaply.

## Recommendation

**Reconsider scope** — ship the expand phase now (new column dual-written, versioned payload accepted in both shapes) and leave dropping `body` and v1 support to the contract follow-up once the v1 counter reads zero; see Q1 and Decision 1 [confidence: medium] [anchor: weighing: risk — tasks enqueued before the deploy are delivered after it, and deploy.sh applies no migrations].

**Redundancy:** none found

## Plan risks

The plan depends on a manual operator step order (back up, apply 002, deploy, re-apply 002) that nothing in `deploy.sh` enforces; if 002 is skipped before the deploy, every report read and every section save fails on the new revision.

## Cut list

- The duration histogram, failures counter and SLO are not needed for the rename itself; only the payload-version counter is load-bearing here (it says when v1 support can go). Cut Task 5's histogram and failures counter if the reviewer wants the minimal diff.
- The enqueue timeout and status check guard a producer with no caller in this repo; they are cheap but could be dropped without affecting any in-repo path.

# Task breakdown

### Task 1: Migration 002 — add and backfill `content`

- **Skill:** `flow-system-design`
- **Description:** Create the expand-phase migration. Idempotent so the same file is run before the deploy and again after the new revision serves 100% of traffic. Header comment carries the operator runbook: (1) `gcloud sql backups create --instance <instance>`; (2) `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f migrations/002_sections_content.sql`; (3) `./deploy.sh`; (4) re-run step 2; (5) restore check `select count(*) from sections where content is distinct from body` returns 0. It must state that re-running is only valid while dual-write is live.
- **Inputs:** migrations/001_reports.sql
- **Outputs:** an additive, re-runnable migration
- **Contract:**
  - **Files:** `migrations/002_sections_content.sql` (create)
  - **Interfaces:** DDL —
    - `alter table sections add column if not exists content text;`
    - `update sections set content = body where content is distinct from body;`
  - **Call-site edits:** none
- **Acceptance criteria:** `grep -q 'add column if not exists content text' migrations/002_sections_content.sql && grep -q 'is distinct from body' migrations/002_sections_content.sql && ! grep -qiE '\b(rename|drop)\b' migrations/002_sections_content.sql`

### Task 2: Id-keyed persistence with dual-write

- **Skill:** `flow-new-feature`
- **Description:** Add id lookup and id-keyed save; every write sets both `content` and `body`; reads serve `coalesce(content, body)` under the existing `body` key (Q2). Rename the name-keyed save to mark it legacy and update its single call site.
- **Inputs:** Task 1's column; src/db.ts
- **Outputs:** persistence API used by the worker
- **Contract:**
  - **Files:** `src/db.ts` (edit), `src/worker.ts` (edit, one call site)
  - **Interfaces:**
    - `export type Section = { id: string; report_id: string; name: string }`
    - `export async function getSection(id: string): Promise<Section | undefined>` — `select id, report_id, name from sections where id = ${id}`
    - `export async function listSections(reportId: string)` — `select id, name, coalesce(content, body) as body from sections where report_id = ${reportId} order by position`
    - `export async function saveSectionContent(id: string, content: string): Promise<void>` — `update sections set content = ${content}, body = ${content} where id = ${id}`
    - `export async function saveSectionContentByName(reportId: string, name: string, content: string): Promise<void>` — legacy v1, same dual-write `where report_id = ${reportId} and name = ${name}`; replaces `saveSection`
  - **Call-site edits:** `src/worker.ts` `handleGenerateSection`: `saveSection(...)` → `saveSectionContentByName(...)`
- **Acceptance criteria:** `grep -q 'coalesce(content, body) as body' src/db.ts && ! grep -q 'saveSection(' src/worker.ts && bun build src/app.ts --target bun --outfile /tmp/reports-build.js`

### Task 3: Model-call timeout and error guard

- **Skill:** `flow-system-design`
- **Bundled:** missing timeout on the paid model call, and non-2xx answers saved as blank section text, both on the path this plan edits
- **Description:** Give `generateSection` a 120 s abort (Q5) and throw on non-2xx or missing `text`, so the worker reports a transient failure instead of saving nothing. Export a typed error so the worker maps it to `upstream_error` / `upstream_timeout`.
- **Inputs:** src/llm.ts
- **Outputs:** a bounded, failing-loudly model call
- **Contract:**
  - **Files:** `src/llm.ts` (edit)
  - **Interfaces:**
    - `export const GENERATE_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000`
    - `export class UpstreamError extends Error { constructor(readonly kind: "upstream_error" | "upstream_timeout", message: string) }`
    - `export async function generateSection(company: string, section: string): Promise<string>` — same signature; `fetch(..., { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(GENERATE_TIMEOUT_MS) })`; `TimeoutError` → `UpstreamError("upstream_timeout")`; `!res.ok` or non-string `text` → `UpstreamError("upstream_error")`
  - **Call-site edits:** none (signature unchanged)
- **Acceptance criteria:** `grep -q 'AbortSignal.timeout(GENERATE_TIMEOUT_MS)' src/llm.ts && bun build src/llm.ts --target bun --outfile /tmp/llm-build.js`

### Task 4: Versioned task payload (producer)

- **Skill:** `flow-system-design`
- **Bundled:** enqueue call had no timeout and ignored a failed Cloud Tasks response; the queue had no dispatch deadline or max attempts, which matters now that model errors retry instead of being marked done

    - `export async function enqueueSection(reportId: string, section: { id: string; name: string }): Promise<void>` — body `btoa(JSON.stringify(buildGenerateSectionTask(...)))`, task field `dispatchDeadline: "300s"`, `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)`, throws on `!res.ok`
    - `deploy.sh` config: after the `queues create` line add `gcloud tasks queues update sections --location us-central1 --max-attempts=5 --min-backoff=10s --max-backoff=300s` (before: no retry settings; after: dispatch deadline 300 s per task, max attempts 5)

# PR description draft

## TLDR

Section generation jobs now find their section by id where before they matched a non-unique name, and section text moves to a new field, staged so reports and queued jobs keep working mid-deploy.

## User-facing changes

- Report reads look the same: each section still arrives with its text under `body`, now served from the new `content` field.
- A section whose generation fails now gets retried instead of being saved blank:
  - **Before:** a model error saved empty text and the job counted as done.
  - **After:** the job fails, the queue retries it, and the section fills once a call succeeds.
- A generation that hangs is now abandoned after 120 seconds and retried:
  - **Before:** a hung call held the job until the queue's 10-minute deadline.
  - **After:** the call stops at 120 seconds and the queue retries it.

## System changes

- Section text moves to a new column, with the old one kept as a mirror:
  - **Before:** section text lived only in `body`.
  - **After:** `content` is the column of record and `body` is written in lockstep until the follow-up drops it.
- The generate-section job now carries the section id:
  - **Before:** jobs carried the report id and section name, and saving matched every section with that name, or none.
  - **After:** jobs carry a version, the section id and, for one release, the name; the worker finds exactly one section by id before paying for a call, and still handles old name-only jobs.
- Each job is now capped at five attempts with a five-minute deadline per attempt, so a failing section costs at most five paid calls; jobs for deleted sections no longer pay for a call at all.
- The worker records duration, failures and job-version counts; the old-version count reaching zero is the signal that the follow-up can remove the legacy path.

## Why

Section text sits under a field name that no longer fits, and generation jobs find their section by display name, which is not unique and can match nothing while the job still reports success. The database change is applied by hand, separately from the deploy, and jobs queued before a deploy are delivered after it, so a direct swap would break report reads and drop or repeat paid generations during the rollout.

## Key decisions

- Staged rename instead of an in-place rename: an in-place rename leaves minutes where reads fail and paid jobs retry, and breaks rollback.
- The report API keeps its `body` key; renaming a public field needs its own client migration.
- The job keeps the section name for one release next to the id, so a rollback to the previous version can still process new jobs.
- Operator order: back up, apply the new migration, deploy, re-apply the migration once the new revision serves all traffic.
- Dropping the old column and the old job shape is a follow-up, gated on the old-version job count reading zero.
- Bundled: timeout and error guard on the paid model call, which previously saved blank text on failure.
- Bundled: timeout and status check on the job enqueue call, plus a per-job deadline and a five-attempt retry cap on the queue.
- Bundled: no paid model call for a section that no longer exists.

## Instrumentation

- New metrics: section-generation duration by outcome, failures by error type, and generate-section jobs by payload version; queue depth comes from Cloud Tasks itself.
- Panels added to the `reports-service overview` dashboard: duration, failures, jobs by version, queue depth. Spec-only: no dashboard URL exists yet.
- New SLO: section generation, 99% of jobs succeed over 28 days, excluding deleted or invalid jobs; burn-rate alerts only.
- This PR creates the metrics contract with no backend chosen yet (suggested: Google Cloud Monitoring), so the metrics are recorded in memory and won't show on any graph until a backend is picked.

## Test Steps

<!-- flow:authoring-rubric — for each checkbox item below, the three-question
automation test from manual-test-rubric.md is: (a) named fixture/setup,
(b) deterministic assertion(s), (c) exit condition. If all three are answerable
without subjective human judgment, it must be a runnable item. Source of truth:
skills/pipeline/flow-pr-review/references/manual-test-rubric.md. -->

- [ ] Run `bun test src/worker.test.ts src/queue.test.ts src/llm.test.ts` — all specs pass, covering id-keyed jobs, legacy name-keyed jobs, deleted and mismatched sections, invalid payloads, and model timeouts and errors.
- [ ] Start a throwaway Postgres with `docker run -d --rm --name reports-pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pg -p 55432:5432 postgres:16 && sleep 5`.
- [ ] Run `psql postgresql://postgres:pg@localhost:55432/postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f migrations/001_reports.sql -c "insert into reports(id, company) values ('r1','Acme'); insert into sections(id, report_id, name, position, body) values ('s1','r1','Intro',1,'hello')" -f migrations/002_sections_content.sql -f migrations/002_sections_content.sql` — exits 0, proving 002 is re-runnable.
- [ ] Run `[ "$(psql postgresql://postgres:pg@localhost:55432/postgres -tAc "select count(*) from sections where content is distinct from body")" = "0" ]` — the backfill copied every row.
- [ ] Run `[ "$(psql postgresql://postgres:pg@localhost:55432/postgres -tAc "select coalesce(content, body) as body from sections where id = 's1'")" = "hello" ]` — the read the report API uses returns the text.
- [ ] Run `docker stop reports-pg` — removes the throwaway database.
- [ ] Run `! grep -qiE '\b(rename|drop)\b' migrations/002_sections_content.sql` — the migration is additive, so the previous revision keeps working while it is applied.
